He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee Volunteers]]. ==Early life== Schofield, the son of Anthony and Dawn Schofield, was born at [[St Mary's Hospital, London|St Mary's Hospital]] in London.{{Cite web |url=http://www.jsonline.com/sports/badgers/67837037.html |title=An inspirational journey: UW's Schofield motivated after loss of his brother |last=Potrykus, Jeff |date=October 30, 2009 |website=[[Journal Sentinel]] |access-date=January 20, 2014}} His father served in the [[United States Navy]] which required his family to travel.{{cite web |last1=Hotz |first1=Tyler |title=Basketball, Service Enable Schofield to Tour the Globe |url=https://utsports.com/news/2017/6/22/mens-basketball-basketball-service-enable-schofield-to-tour-the-globe |website=University of Tennessee Athletics |access-date=December 26, 2024 |date=June 22, 2017}} His brother [[O'Brien Schofield]] is a linebacker who won a Super Bowl with the [[Seattle Seahawks]]. He has another brother General and a sister Octavia; one other brother, Joshua, drowned in [[Lake Michigan]] in 2007. Schofield moved with his family to [[Illinois]] as a one-year-old. Schofield attended [[Zion-Benton High School]] where he played center. In his final high school game, he recorded 23 points with 18 rebounds against Stevenson in the Class 4A regional championship. In [[Amateur Athletic Union|AAU]] play, he competed for Dickey Simpkins' Team NLP. [[Donnie Tyndall]] recruited him to Tennessee, but Schofield decided to stay after Tyndall was fired. ==College career== Schofield averaged 7.6 points and 4.0 rebounds per game as a freshman. He missed three games as a sophomore while he was suspended for violating team rules.{{Cite web |last=Rutherford |first=Nathanael |date=2019-03-05 |title=Vols' Seniors are Testament to Tennessee's Culture and Development |url=https://www.rockytopinsider.com/2019/03/05/vols-seniors-are-testament-to-tennessees-culture-and-development/ |access-date=2024-03-08 |website=Rocky Top Insider |language=en-US}} He only scored 3.5 points per game in nonconference play, but began to break out during the conference season and had his first double-double of 18 points and 10 rebounds in a loss to [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]].{{Cite news |url=http://www.timesfreepress.com/news/sports/college/story/2017/jan/18/admiral-schofield-now-playing-vols-want-and-e/408081/ |title=Admiral Schofield now playing like Vols 'want and expect |last=Brown |first=Patrick |date=January 18, 2017 |work=[[Times Free Press]] |access-date=May 20, 2018}} As a sophomore at Tennessee, Schofield averaged 8.2 points and 4.4 rebounds per game.{{Cite news |url=http://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/college/ct-spt-loyola-tennessee-admiral-schofield-20180316-story.html |title=Zion-Benton product Admiral Schofield out to help Tennessee sink Loyola |last=Ryan |first=Shannon |date=March 17, 2018 |work=[[Chicago Tribune]] |access-date=May 20, 2018}} Schofield was named to the SEC All-Tournament Team as a junior due to a 22-point effort in the SEC Title game loss to [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]].{{Cite news |url=https://www.thedailytimes.com/test/schofield-declares-for-draft-without-hiring-agent/article_1b2b99b0-bf59-5fc3-be85-74502d13f5bf.html |title=Schofield declares for draft without hiring agent |last=White |first=Taylor |date=March 30, 2018 |work=[[The Daily Times (Blount County, Tennessee)|The Daily Times]] |access-date=May 20, 2018 }}{{Dead link|date=August 2023 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} As a junior, Schofield averaged 13.9 points and 6.5 rebounds per game. He helped Tennessee to a 26–9 record and the second round of the NCAA tournament. In the first round win over [[Wright State Raiders men's basketball|Wright State]], Schofield had 15 points and 12 rebounds. Schofield was named to the Second Team All-[[Southeastern Conference|SEC]]. Following the season, he declared for the [[2018 NBA draft]] but did not hire an agent, thus leaving open the possibility of returning to the Volunteers.{{Cite news |url=https://www.knoxnews.com/story/sports/college/university-of-tennessee/mens-basketball/2018/03/29/tennessee-vols-basketball-admiral-schofield-nba-draft-agent-rick-barnes-mock-draft-ut-sec-hoops/471409002/ |title=Tennessee Vols forward Admiral Schofield will enter name in NBA draft but won't hire agent |last=Toppmeyer |first=Blake |date=March 29, 2018 |work=[[Knoxville News-Sentinel]] |access-date=May 20, 2018}} Schofield announced his return to Tennessee on May 29.{{Cite news |url=https://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2018/05/29/admiral-schofields-return-sets-up-tennessee-for-big-2018-19-season/ |title=Admiral Schofield's return sets up Tennessee for big 2018–19 season |last=Johnson |first=Raphielle |date=May 29, 2018 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |access-date=May 30, 2018}} As a senior, Schofield averaged 16.5 points and 6.1 rebounds per game.{{Cite news |url=https://www.wbir.com/article/sports/college/vols/grant-williams-admiral-schofield-earn-ap-all-american-honors/51-4f282e9c-0501-4fa6-b87c-b05012a9c53b |title=Grant Williams, Admiral Schofield earn AP All-American honors |date=April 2, 2019 |work=WBIR |access-date=April 4, 2019}} He was named to the First Team All-SEC.{{Cite press release |title=2019 SEC Men's Basketball Awards announced |date=March 12, 2019 |publisher=Southeaster Conference |url=http://www.secsports.com/article/26238088/2019-sec-men-basketball-awards-announced |access-date=March 12, 2019}} He led Tennessee to a 31–6 record and the Sweet 16 of the NCAA tournament. In his final career game, a 99–94 overtime loss to [[Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball|Purdue]], Schofield finished with 21 points.{{Cite news |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401123382 |title=Elite Eight-bound: Purdue holds off Tennessee 99-94 in OT |date=March 29, 2019 |work=[[ESPN]] |access-date=April 4, 2019 |agency=[[Associated Press]]}} ==Professional career== ===Washington Wizards (2019–2020)=== [[File:Admiral Schofield Wizards.jpg|thumb|left|Schofield in 2020]] Schofield was selected in the second round of the [[2019 NBA draft]] by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]], then immediately traded to the [[Washington Wizards]].{{cite news |last1=Brook |first1=Zach |title=Wizards' Admiral Schofield is already one of the NBA's most interesting rookies |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/washington/wizards/wizards-admiral-schofield-already-one-nbas-most-interesting-rookies |access-date=December 12, 2019 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |date=June 26, 2019}} He signed a three-year, $4.3 million contract with the Wizards in July. Schofield became a pitchman for [[Hulu]] Sports in August.{{cite news |last1=Taylor |first1=Cody |title=Wizards' Admiral Schofield shoots his shot, lands ad deal with Hulu |url=https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/2019/08/28/washington-wizards-admiral-schofield-hulu-endorsement-deal-online-streaming-live-sports/ |access-date=December 12, 2019 |work=Rookie Wire |date=August 28, 2019}} Schofield was assigned to the [[NBA G League]] team the [[Capital City Go-Go]]. On December 4, he became the first player in the Wizards organization to play a game for the Go-Go and Wizards in the same day.{{cite news |last1=Hughes |first1=Chase |title=How playing two games in a day went for Wizards rookie Admiral Schofield |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/washington/wizards/how-playing-two-games-day-went-wizards-rookie-admiral-schofield |access-date=December 12, 2019 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |date=December 4, 2019}} On January 8, 2020, Schofield had 18 points, six rebounds and two assists off the bench in a 123–89 loss to the [[Orlando Magic]].{{cite news |title=Wizards' Admiral Schofield: Impressive showing off bench |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/327884-wizards-admiral-schofield-impressive-showing-off-bench/ |access-date=January 16, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=January 9, 2020}} Prior to the stoppage of the NBA season, Schofield played 27 games for the Wizards, averaging 3.1 points and 1.3 rebounds in 10.9 minutes per game, shooting 40.0 percent from the floor. In the G League, he started all 33 games for the Go-Go, averaging 16.0 points, 5.5 rebounds and 2.0 assists in 30.9 minutes per game.{{cite news |last1=Ramey |first1=Grant |title=Admiral Schofield talks NBA stoppage, uncertain future |url=https://247sports.com/college/tennessee/LongFormArticle/Tennessee-Vols-Basketball-Admiral-Schofield-talks-NBA-stoppage-uncertain-future-145236856/ |access-date=April 11, 2020 |work=247 Sports |date=March 30, 2020}} ===Greensboro Swarm (2021)=== On November 19, 2020, Schofield was traded to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] along with [[Vít Krejčí]] for [[Cassius Winston]] and a 2024 second-round pick.{{cite web|title=Thunder Acquires Admiral Schofield and Draft Rights to Vít Krejčí|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/schofield-krejci-201119|website=NBA.com|date=November 19, 2020|access-date=September 23, 2021}} However, he was waived by the Thunder at the end of the preseason.{{Cite web |last=Lay |first=Ken |date=December 29, 2020 |title=Admiral Schofield waived by Oklahoma City |url=https://volswire.usatoday.com/2020/12/29/admiral-schofield-former-vol-waived-oklahoma-city-thunder/ |access-date=December 29, 2020 |website=Vols Wire|publisher=USA Today}} On January 11, 2021, he was selected by the [[Greensboro Swarm]] with the first overall pick of the [[NBA G League]] draft.{{cite web|title=Greensboro Swarm Select Admiral Schofield with First Pick of 2021 NBA G League Draft|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/greensboro-swarm-select-admiral-schofield-with-first-pick-of-2021-nba-g-league-draft/n-5660040|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=January 11, 2021|access-date=January 11, 2021}}{{cite web|title=Greensboro Announces Roster For Single-Site In Orlando|url=https://greensboro.gleague.nba.com/news/greensboro-announces-roster-for-single-site-in-orlando/|website=NBA.com|date=January 27, 2021|access-date=January 27, 2021}} In 14 games, he averaged 10.1 points, 5.7 rebounds and 2.1 assists in 26.2 minutes per game.{{cite web|title=Orlando Magic Sign Ford, Gravett, Johnson and Schofield to 10-Day Contracts|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/orlando-magic-sign-ford-gravett-johnson-and-schofield-10-day-contracts-20211217|website=NBA.com|date=December 17, 2021|access-date=December 17, 2021}} ===Lakeland Magic (2021)=== In August 2021, Schofield joined the [[Atlanta Hawks]] for the [[2021 NBA summer league|2021 NBA Summer League]], recording no points on 0-3 shooting, 7 rebounds and 4 assists in 25 minutes at his debut, a 85–83 loss against the [[Boston Celtics]].{{cite web|title=Boston Celtics vs Atlanta Hawks Aug 8, 2021 Box Scores {{!}} NBA.com|url=https://www.nba.com/game/bos-vs-atl-1522100001/box-score#box-score|website=NBA.com|access-date=August 8, 2021}} On September 21, 2021, he signed with the [[Orlando Magic]],{{cite web|title=Orlando Magic Sign Admiral Schofield|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/orlando-magic-sign-admiral-schofield-20210921|website=NBA.com|date=September 21, 2021|access-date=September 23, 2021}} but was waived at the end of training camp.{{cite web|title=Orlando Magic Waive Four Players|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/orlando-magic-waive-four-players-20211016|website=NBA.com|date=October 16, 2021|access-date=October 17, 2021}} On October 28, he joined the [[Lakeland Magic]]{{cite web|title=Lakeland Magic 2021-22 Training Camp Roster|url=https://lakeland.gleague.nba.com/news/lakeland-magic-2021-22-training-camp-roster/|website=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2021|access-date=October 28, 2021}} and played 12 games, averaging 14.4 points, 7.2 rebounds and 1.8 assists in 33.0 minutes per game. ===Orlando / Lakeland Magic (2021–2024)=== On December 17, 2021, Schofield signed a 10-day contract with the [[Orlando Magic]]. two-way contract - Orlando also waives Mychal Mulder #MagicTogether t.co/EnKtzEpHi8"|url=https://twitter.com/Magic_PR/status/1479204704991301640|date=January 6, 2022|access-date=January 6, Schofield was fined $20,000 by the NBA for his role in an on-court altercation during a game against the [[Charlotte Hornets]] two days later.{{cite web|title=Magic's Admiral Schofield, Robin Lopez On July 22, 2022, Schofield signed another two-way contract with the Magic.{{cite web|title=Orlando Magic Re-Sign Admiral Schofield to a Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/orlando-magic-re-sign-admiral-schofield-nba-two-way-contract-release-story-20220722|website=NBA.com|date=July 22, 2022|access-date=July 23, 2022}} On December 29, he was suspended by the NBA for one game without pay due to coming off the bench during an altercation in a game against the [[Detroit Pistons]] the day before.{{cite web|title=NBA announces suspensions from Pistons-Magic game|url=https://www.nba.com/news/nba-announces-pistons-magic-suspensions|website=NBA.com|date=December 29, 2022|access-date=December 31, 2022}} On February 21, 2023, the Magic converted Schofield's deal to a standard NBA contract.{{cite web|title=Orlando Magic PR on Twitter: "PRESS RELEASE: @OrlandoMagic convert contract of @admiralelite15 to standard NBA contract #MagicTogether"|url=https://twitter.com/Magic_PR/status/1628125020164657158|website=Twitter.com|date=February 21, 2023|access-date=February 21, 2023}} On July 20, 2023, Schofield signed
